title.value: Do SSL Models Have Déjà Vu? A Case of Unintended Memorization in Self-supervised Learning
title.justification: The title concisely reflects the key subject matter of the paper which explores the unintended memorization phenomenon in self-supervised learning models.
title.quote: Do SSL Models Have Déjà Vu? A Case of Unintended Memorization in Self-supervised Learning

extractions.description: This paper investigates the unintended memorization phenomenon in self-supervised learning (SSL) algorithms, which can memorize specific parts of training images rather than learning generalized representations. The paper highlights privacy risks associated with this memorization and suggests potential mitigation strategies.

primary_category.justification: The paper primarily focuses on the memorization issues and privacy risks associated with SSL models, which do not directly relate to any of the predefined eco-responsible categories.
primary_category.quote: Our study of déjà vu memorization reveals previously unknown privacy risks in SSL models, as well as suggests potential practical mitigation strategies.

secondary_categories.justification: Since the focus of the paper is on understanding and mitigating unintended memorization in SSL models, it does not align with the secondary eco-responsible categories either.
secondary_categories.quote: This may allow an adversary to extract such information from the trained model for targeted individuals.

primary_sub_category.quote: In this work, we aim to evaluate to what extent SSL models memorize the association of specific objects in training images.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The paper's exploration of SSL memorization and privacy is not relevant to the specified sub-categories, leading to a secondary categorization of N/A.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Our results demonstrate that SSL models memorize such associations beyond simple correlation.
